brief.summary: Tip-pooling and gratuity distribution software for small independent restaurants, with built-in guidance that walks managers through setting up their pool rules and running their first payouts.
brief.user: Gabriela Moretti, general manager of Olive & Ember, a 16-person neighborhood trattoria. The owners just bought Kittyline to replace a spreadsheet the previous manager kept. She knows the restaurant's tip practices well but has never used payroll-adjacent software.
brief.moment: It's Monday and Gabriela is running her first weekly tip distribution in Kittyline, which has to reach the payroll provider by Tuesday noon. She finished the first-run setup last week. Now the pool total won't balance: the system shows $214 in card tips 'unassigned' from Friday, and it's warning that one dishwasher's share would put a back-of-house employee over the pool's allowed share for a manager-designated role. brief.data: Restaurant with 16 staff: 7 servers, 2 bartenders, 2 bussers, 1 host, 3 kitchen (1 line cook, 1 prep, 1 dishwasher), and Gabriela, plus 1 shift lead (Marco Delacroix) who sometimes covers floor management. Pool rules from setup: points-based (server 10, bartender 9, busser 5, host 4, kitchen 3), FOH/BOH split 80/20, and managers excluded. Week of Nov 9–15: $11,842.60 in card tips, $1,306 in declared cash tips, 41 shifts and 612.5 tipped hours, imported from the POS and the timeclock. Friday Nov 13 has $214.00 in card tips on 3 checks closed after the last server clocked out. Kittyline's setup checklist is 7 of 9 steps complete, and payroll export setup and state rules confirmation are still open. The help articles include 'Who counts as a manager?' and 'Late-closed checks'.

prompt:
I need the front end for Kittyline. Tip-pooling and gratuity distribution software for small independent restaurants, with built-in guidance that walks managers through setting up their pool rules and running their first payouts.

Who's using it: Gabriela Moretti, general manager of Olive & Ember, a 16-person neighborhood trattoria. The owners just bought Kittyline to replace a spreadsheet the previous manager kept. She knows the restaurant's tip practices well but has never used payroll-adjacent software.

What they're doing right now: It's Monday and Gabriela is running her first weekly tip distribution in Kittyline, which has to reach the payroll provider by Tuesday noon. She finished the first-run setup last week. Now the pool total won't balance: the system shows $214 in card tips 'unassigned' from Friday, and it's warning that one dishwasher's share would put a back-of-house employee over the pool's allowed share for a manager-designated role. She needs to understand what the warning means, whether a shift lead counts as a manager under the state rules the software applies, how cash tips declared at the end of a shift should be entered, and how to fix Friday so the week closes correctly.

What's in the system at this point: Restaurant with 16 staff: 7 servers, 2 bartenders, 2 bussers, 1 host, 3 kitchen (1 line cook, 1 prep, 1 dishwasher), and Gabriela, plus 1 shift lead (Marco Delacroix) who sometimes covers floor management. Pool rules from setup: points-based (server 10, bartender 9, busser 5, host 4, kitchen 3), FOH/BOH split 80/20, and managers excluded. Week of Nov 9–15: $11,842.60 in card tips, $1,306 in declared cash tips, 41 shifts and 612.5 tipped hours, imported from the POS and the timeclock. Friday Nov 13 has $214.00 in card tips on 3 checks closed after the last server clocked out. Kittyline's setup checklist is 7 of 9 steps complete, and payroll export setup and state rules confirmation are still open. The help articles include 'Who counts as a manager?' and 'Late-closed checks'.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
